qs.q: A patient with small cell lung cancer develops hyponatremia with concentrated urine. The ectopic hormone responsible is ---
qs.e: Small cell lung cancer frequently causes SIADH through ectopic production of antidiuretic hormone.

qs.q: A patient with Small Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC) has anti-VGCC antibodies, weakness that improves with repeated use. What is the diagnosis?
qs.e: LEMS is characterized by anti-VGCC antibodies that impair presynaptic ACh release. Strength paradoxically improves with repeated stimulation — the opposite of Myasthenia Gravis.

qs.q: A 65-year-old man with small-cell lung cancer develops hyponatraemia (Na⁺ 118 mmol/L), urine osmolality 520 mOsm/kg and euvolaemia. Which ectopic hormone production BEST explains this?
qs.e: SIADH from ectopic ADH secretion is the classic paraneoplastic syndrome of SCLC, giving euvolaemic hyponatraemia with high urine osmolality and low serum osmolality. PTHrP causes hypercalcaemia; ectopic ACTH causes Cushing's features.

es.m: The most likely histological subtype of lung cancer in a non-smoking woman is Adenocarcinoma. Small Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC) is almost always metastatic at presentation. It is treated with chemotherapy, and typically has a poor prognosis with a median survival of approximately 1 year.

es.q: A 70-year-old patient is diagnosed with Small Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC). Discuss the typical clinical presentation, treatment approach, and prognosis for this cancer subtype as described in the article.
es.m: Small Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC) is almost always metastatic at presentation (2 marks). Due to its widespread nature, it is typically treated with chemotherapy (1 mark). The prognosis is poor, with a median survival of approximately 1 year (2 marks).

es.m: 1. **Prevalence & Demographics:** Adenocarcinoma is the most common lung cancer subtype overall, and notably, it is the most common type found in women and nonsmokers. ai.subject: Pathology
ai.summary: Small cell lung cancer is a neuroendocrine tumour that grows rapidly, metastasises early and is strongly linked to smoking. It often presents with paraneoplastic syndromes such as SIADH, Cushing’s, or Lambert‑Eaton myasthenic syndrome.

sections.p: SCLC is a malignant tumour of pulmonary neuroendocrine cells, usually central, that shows small, round cells with scant cytoplasm and neuroendocrine markers on immunohistochemistry.

t.b: Detects central tumour and nodal disease; a mass >1 cm in the hilar region suggests SCLC
Obtains tissue for histology and immunostaining; confirms neuroendocrine phenotype
Hyponatraemia with low plasma osmolality and concentrated urine indicates SIADH, a common paraneoplastic sign

sections.p: SCLC is staged as limited (confined to one hemithorax) or extensive (beyond one hemithorax or distant metastasis).
The single most important risk factor is tobacco smoke. Other factors include occupational exposures and possibly viral infections.
Patients often have a central cough, haemoptysis, or dyspnoea. Paraneoplastic syndromes may dominate the initial presentation.
b: Cushing’s: moon facies, proximal muscle weakness

sections.p: The work‑up focuses on confirming the tumour, staging, and detecting paraneoplastic effects.

t.b: Assesses metabolic activity and distant spread
Elevated ACTH with normal pituitary imaging suggests ectopic source
Hyponatraemia with concentrated urine indicates SIADH

sections.p: Rapid progression, early metastasis, and paraneoplastic syndromes can be life‑threatening.
b: SIADH can lead to severe hyponatraemia and cerebral oedema

sections.p: SCLC is chemosensitive but rarely curable; treatment is systemic and supportive.
b: Platinum (cisplatin or carboplatin) + etoposide – first‑line chemotherapy
Concurrent thoracic radiotherapy in limited stage
Supportive care: anti‑emetics, growth factors, pain control

sections.p: Regular imaging to detect recurrence and counselling to stop smoking.
b: CT chest every 3–6 months for 2 years

sections.p: Other central lung tumours and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma.
b: Large cell carcinoma – similar appearance but less neuroendocrine markers
Squamous cell carcinoma – usually peripheral and keratinising

sections.p: Some tests may be falsely normal early in disease.
b: Early CT may miss small hilar nodules
Serum sodium can be normal if SIADH is intermittent

whenToSeekHelp: Severe hyponatraemia with confusion or seizures
New onset muscle weakness or autonomic instability

faq.q: Why is smoking the biggest risk factor?
faq.a: Tobacco smoke contains carcinogens that cause DNA mutations in neuroendocrine cells, leading to malignant transformation.
Only in very early limited disease; most patients have metastatic disease at diagnosis and treatment is palliative.

faq.q: What is the role of surgery?
faq.a: Surgery is rarely used because the tumour is usually metastatic at presentation and responds better to chemotherapy.
